_comment: Resources AMDG shares with the wider research community. 'instrumentHeading' labels the compact College of Engineering & Computer Science instrument grid. 'instruments' render in array order; 'photos' are optional /images/... paths and only resolved files render, 'sponsor' matches the project-card agency badge, and 'toolsAfter' places the web-tools grid immediately after the featured instrument. 'tools' contain web apps: 'name' and 'description' are required; 'url' renders a link line (omit it while a tool is in beta); 'status' renders a small pill (colors live in STATUS_COLORS in ResourceCard.astro).
instrumentHeading: AMDG hosts the following resources for the Department of Mechanical Engineering and the College of Engineering & Computer Science. These resources are available to all University of Tulsa researchers. Contact us to coordinate access, training, etc.

tools.name: digitalimagecorrelation.org
tools.description: A practical guide to digital image correlation, written for newcomers. It covers speckle patterning, image capture, calibration, and error validation, and surveys the available open-source DIC software.

tools.name: e2283.app
tools.description: Extreme value analysis of inclusion lengths following ASTM E2283. Enter 24 measurements and the app returns a Gumbel fit, for use by the fatigue community.

tools.name: PreCureSim
tools.description: Simulation of curing and yield for preceramic polymers.

instruments.name: Psylotech µTS
instruments.description: A compact tensile testing system that can operate inside of a scanning electron microscope, as well as outside with optical microscopes and a 1600°C air furnace. It can pull up to 1.6 kN and can run fatigue tests at tens of Hz and hundreds of N.

photos.alt: The Psylotech µTS compact mechanical testing system.

instruments.sponsorNote: Funding: NSF Major Research Instrumentation award no. 2320690.
instruments.access: The µTS is open for use by anyone in the U.S. research community. To discuss access, contact Prof. William LePage.

instruments.name: Legolas — Instron ElectroPuls E3000
instruments.description: Electrodynamic load frame with 3 kN and 100+ Hz capacity. Features closed-loop feedback and auto-tuning with force and strain, along with sample temperature monitoring. Supports pneumatic grips for samples up to 0.25 inch thick or round. Includes a 6000 VA Li-ion battery backup for uninterrupted tests during power outages.

photos.alt: A student threads a specimen into the grips of the Instron E3000 while a second student looks on.

instruments.name: Gimli — Instron 34TM-30
instruments.description: 30 kN electromechanical load frame with extensive and advanced digital image correlation capabilities (stereo or 2D, live strain feedback/control, cross-polarized blue light, and with lenses suitable to samples with gauge section sizes from about 50 microns to 500 mm). Features wedge-action grips suitable for samples up to 0.25 inches thick and 1 inch wide, as well as multiple load cells (10 N, 500 N, 5 kN, and 30 kN).

photos.alt: Two researchers at the Gimli control station, with live load–displacement data and a DIC image of the specimen on the monitors.

instruments.name: Keyence VHX-X1F
instruments.description: Digital microscope equipped with a ZMT metallurgical lens, polarized illumination, differential image contrast, and 100×, 200×, 400×, and 1000× objectives. Automated stitching combines adjacent fields of view and images captured at different focal depths to produce large-area, fully focused images and 3D surface reconstructions.

photos.alt: Two students inspect a micrograph on the Keyence digital microscope display.
